objective_for_doctor: A 58-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have swollen or painful lymph nodes, sensitive pain, and sharp pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Hi doctor. I’ve had swollen and painful lymph nodes, with sensitive and sharp pain. It started kind of gradually, and right now the pain is about 4 out of 10, mostly localized where the nodes are.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—thanks. When did this start, and do you have fever, night sweats, weight loss, recent infections, or any new lumps elsewhere?  
Doctor: Also, are the swollen nodes in the neck, armpit, or groin, and are you noticing skin redness/warmth or dental/throat symptoms?

It started gradually, like over a short time, about 1 out of 10 for how fast it came on. I don’t have fever, night sweats, or weight loss that I’ve noticed, and I haven’t had any recent infections or new lumps elsewhere.  

The swollen nodes are in my neck (not armpit or groin). I don’t have skin redness or warmth, and no dental or throat symptoms.

Doctor: Any recent dental issues (gum pain, tooth problems), sore throat, cough, or sinus symptoms—even mild—plus do you feel the neck node is movable vs fixed, and about what size (e.g., pea/bean/grape)?  
Doctor: Also, are you a smoker, and have you had prior head/neck radiation or a history of lymphoma?

No dental problems, no sore throat, cough, or sinus symptoms. The neck node feels tender and sensitive, but I’m not sure if it’s fully movable or fixed. I think it’s smaller than a grape—more like pea/bean size.  

I’m not a smoker, and I haven’t had radiation to the head/neck, and no history of lymphoma.

Doctor: Thanks—since it’s tender pea/bean-sized in the neck with gradual onset and no “B symptoms” or infection symptoms, I’d like to check for deeper causes. Do you have recent scalp issues (dandruff/boils), skin rash or insect bites on the head/face, and is it on one side only?  
Doctor: Also, REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential and CRP/ESR.

I don’t have any recent scalp problems like dandruff or boils, and no rash or insect bites on my head or face. I’m not sure if it’s only on one side, but I think it’s mainly in the neck area where I feel the nodes.

Doctor: Any trouble swallowing, hoarseness, ear pain on the same side, or a persistent lump that’s getting bigger over days? Also, any recent travel, animal/tick exposure, or new medications?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound of the neck lymph nodes.

No trouble swallowing, no hoarseness, and no ear pain on that side. The lump hasn’t been getting bigger over days—at least I haven’t noticed it changing. No recent travel, no tick or animal exposure, and no new medications.

Doctor: Thanks—on exam, do you feel it’s a single node or multiple, and is it clearly discrete? Also, does it move more with swallowing or turning your head, and any mouth sores, tongue lesions, or persistent bad breath?

I can feel it as a node in the neck area, but I’m not sure if it’s just one or a few—maybe more than one. It feels fairly discrete. It doesn’t really move a lot with swallowing or turning my head. I don’t have mouth sores, tongue lesions, or persistent bad breath.

Doctor: I’ll examine your neck—can you point to the exact area (right/left, under the jaw vs along the side of the neck), and do you have any numbness, weakness, or new headaches? Also, are you currently taking any antibiotics or NSAIDs, and does the node tenderness change with pain medicines?

It’s on the side of my neck, kind of along the side rather than under the jaw. I don’t have numbness, weakness, or new headaches. I’m not taking antibiotics right now, and I’ve not noticed that it changes much with pain medicines.

Doctor: Thanks—so lateral neck, pea/bean-sized, discrete but possibly multiple nodes, tender, gradual onset, no B symptoms, and no clear infectious source. I’m going to request results to narrow this: REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential and CRP_ESR, plus REQUEST TEST: Ultrasound_of_neck_lymph_nodes (if not already done).  

Doctor: While we wait, do you have any dental issues you might have overlooked (recent tooth sensitivity, gum bleeding), and has the node been present for more than 2–4 weeks or clearly persisting at the same size?

No dental issues that I’ve noticed—no tooth sensitivity or gum bleeding. And the node has been present only for a short time so far; I can’t say it’s been more than 2–4 weeks, and I think it’s been about the same size.

Doctor: Based on what we’ve discussed—tender pea/bean-sized lateral neck nodes, discrete, short duration, no fever/weight loss, and no clear throat/dental source—this most commonly fits reactive/inflammatory cervical lymphadenitis, though we should still rule out atypical infection or lymphoma if it persists.  

Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Neck_lymph_node_ultrasound (with Doppler) and REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential + CRP_ESR (if not already completed); if ultrasound suggests benign/reactive pattern and labs are reassuring, we’ll treat conservatively and recheck in 2–4 weeks.
Okay, doctor. That plan makes sense to me—I’m okay with getting the ultrasound and blood tests, and I can come back for a recheck in 2–4 weeks if needed.

Doctor: Great—while we’re arranging the ultrasound and CBC/CRP/ESR, can you tell me your current temperature and whether the pain is improving, worsening, or staying the same over the past few days?  
Doctor: Also, any recent viral symptoms at all (even mild), and do you have enlarged nodes anywhere else besides the neck?

I don’t know my exact temperature right now. The pain feels about the same, not really improving or worsening over the past few days.  

No recent viral symptoms that I’ve noticed, and I only have enlarged nodes in the neck—nowhere else.

Doctor: Got it—stable tender lateral cervical nodes, no other lymphadenopathy, and no viral symptoms. I’m going to request/confirm results now: REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential + CRP_ESR, and REQUEST TEST: Neck_lymph_node_ultrasound (with Doppler). Based on your pattern so far, the leading diagnosis is reactive/inflammatory cervical lymphadenitis, but we’ll confirm by ultrasound and labs.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive/inflammatory cervical lymphadenitis (likely), pending ultrasound and CBC/CRP/ESR confirmation.
